answer: To open a seat, an agent must lease one week of a rural radio shed, bury a uniquely cored umber-clay witness brick in the shed floor, and at an unannounced hour transmit a live Morse signal whose timing is taken from a thermocouple on a small charcoal ember kept in a sealed stove. Shared sheds, reused brick cores, or a replayed recording without a live ember are slashed as one operator. Fielding N identities therefore costs N shed-weeks, N surveyed umber cores, and N live stoves that cannot be fed from a single furnace or a copied tape.
